# How to translate a letter or document into plain English with any AI

> **In short:** Paste the foreign text (or its scan) into any AI assistant, ask for a faithful plain-English version that preserves tone and key dates, then verify the critical numbers. Free tools handle short letters; longer or sensitive documents may need a paid plan or a human translator for legal weight.

Imagine a thick envelope lands on your kitchen table — a notice from a foreign agency, an email from a relative abroad, a scanned rental contract from a trip. Your stomach drops a little because the words aren't yours. The good news: in 2026, you can turn almost any foreign-language letter or document into clean English in minutes, and you don't need to be technical to do it. This guide walks you through the process with any major AI assistant — ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Copilot, Le Chat, or DeepSeek — using the same five moves.

## Before you start
- **Any AI assistant** you already have an account with (ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Copilot, Le Chat, DeepSeek — all work the same way for this task). Free plans are fine for short letters.
- **The original text** — typed out, copied from an email, or a clear photo/scan. Blurry scans slow everything down.
- **Roughly 10 minutes** for the first try; about 3 minutes once you've done it twice.
- *Honest heads-up:* an AI translation is great for understanding what it means. It is **not** a certified translation — for official or court purposes you'll still need a sworn human translator.

## Step 1 — Get the text into a clean, copyable form
Open the letter, email, or scanned document and get its words into a form you can copy. For digital text, highlight it all and copy. For a paper letter or PDF scan, open your phone's camera app (or a scanner app like the one that came preinstalled) and take a straight, well-lit photo — flat on the table, no shadows, no fingers in the shot. On most phones, the built-in scanner detects the page automatically; if not, look for a button labeled something like **Scan**, **Capture**, or **Document** in your camera or Notes app.
💬 Example: photograph a single A4 page top-down on a dark table, with a desk lamp to the side — not behind you, which causes glare.
You'll know it worked when the page edges form a clean rectangle on screen and you can tap **Save** or **Copy text**.

## Step 2 — Open your AI assistant and paste the text
Open the assistant of your choice in a browser or app, start a new chat, and paste the text into the message box. If you have a scan instead, tap the **paperclip** or **attachment icon** next to the message box and choose your photo or PDF. A small thumbnail appears next to your message. If your app shows a different icon for attachments, look for one shaped like a **plus sign (+)** or a **picture icon** — most assistants tuck uploads behind one of those. Hit **Send** or the **up-arrow** button.
💬 Example: paste 200 words of a German utility letter, or attach one JPG of a Spanish rental contract.
You'll know it worked when the assistant confirms it received the text — usually a short reply like "Got it" or it just starts answering.

## Step 3 — Ask for a faithful, plain-English version with key details preserved
In the same chat, type a short instruction that tells the assistant three things: (1) translate the full content, (2) keep the original tone (formal stays formal, friendly stays friendly), and (3) preserve any dates, names, amounts, deadlines, and reference numbers exactly as written. Send it. Most assistants will return a clear English version within seconds.
💬 Example: *"Please translate this letter into plain English. Keep the tone the same as the original (formal/polite). Keep all dates, names, addresses, account numbers, and amounts exactly as they appear — do not round or reformat them."*
You'll know it worked when you see a clean English paragraph (or several) that reads naturally and the numbers match the source exactly.

## Step 4 — Ask for a short summary of what action, if any, is needed
This is the step most people skip — and it's the one that saves you from missing a deadline. Add a second message asking the assistant to summarize, in three or four bullet points: what the sender wants, what you must do (if anything), by when, and what happens if you don't. Some assistants call this a "TL;DR" or "key takeaways" — the wording you use doesn't matter, the idea does.
💬 Example: *"Now give me 3–4 short bullets: (1) what the sender wants, (2) what I need to do, (3) by when, (4) what happens if I do nothing."*
You'll know it worked when the reply ends in numbered or bulleted lines and you can answer the question "what should I do next?" without rereading the full translation.

## Step 5 — Verify the critical details before you act
Read the summary first, then the full translation. Cross-check every date, name, address, account number, and amount against the original — these are the items AI most often mistypes or "smooths over." If something is off, ask the assistant to redo it: *"Please re-check item 3 — the amount should be 1,240 EUR, not 1,420."* For anything legal, medical, or financial that you'll act on, treat the AI output as a draft you double-check, not as the final word.
💬 Example: spot-check the deadline date and the account/IBAN number first; those are the two mistakes that cause the most real-world pain.
You'll know it worked when every important number matches the original and you feel confident telling a friend "this letter says I have until June 14 to respond."

## Common mistakes
- **Pasting a blurry photo of text instead of a clean scan.** The assistant will guess, and guesses on numbers are dangerous. Retake the photo flat on a table with even lighting.
- **Asking only for "a translation" without asking to preserve tone and details.** You'll get a clean-sounding version that quietly dropped the deadline or the account number. Always include the three-part instruction from Step 3.
- **Trusting the translation on legal, medical, or financial documents without a human check.** AI is excellent at understanding meaning; it is not a certified translator. For anything that goes to a court, a tax office, or a hospital, use a sworn human translator for the final version.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** the next time a foreign bank, utility, school, or relative sends you something, you'll read it in English in under five minutes — and you'll know what (if anything) you need to do about it.
- **For your business or work:** use the same five moves to triage incoming foreign-language invoices, contracts, and supplier emails. The summary step alone can save an hour of "what does this actually want from me?" thinking per message.
- **If you're just getting started:** try it once this week on any small piece of foreign text you have lying around — an old email, a product manual, a menu. The first one takes ten minutes; the second one takes three.

## Try it now
Pick one short piece of foreign-language text in your email or on your desk right now — even a single paragraph is enough. Open your usual AI assistant, paste it in, and send the Step 3 prompt word-for-word. Read the summary it gives you, then decide what (if anything) you'd actually do about it. That's the whole skill, and you now have it.
